podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: One-Off Band for a Single Show – Late August 1978
podcast.body: Sid Vicious put this band together and played only one show at the Electric Ballroom in London in late August 1978. The lineup included Rat Scabies of The Damned on drums and Glenn Matlock, the Sex Pistols' former bassist, on bass, with Sid on vocals. "Sid put together a band and played one show at the Electric Ballroom in London in late August of 1978."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Funding for New York Move – Gig Money and McLaren Loan
podcast.body: The money earned from the Electric Ballroom gig, combined with a £10,000 loan (in £10 notes) from Malcolm McLaren, funded Sid and Nancy's flight to New York City. "With the money from that gig at the Electric Ballroom in a 10,000-pound loan from Malcolm McLaren... Sid and Nancy flew to New York City."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fundraising Gig for New York Move
podcast.body: Formed as a temporary group featuring Sid Vicious on vocals, Glenn Matlock (whom Sid had replaced in the Sex Pistols) on bass, Rats Scabies of The Damned on drums, and Steve New on guitar, this group played a quick solo gig at the Electric Ballroom in Camden on August 15, 1978. The purpose was to raise money for Sid and Nancy to fly to New York. "To raise money, there was a quick solo gig at the electric ballroom in Camden under the name Vicious White Kids."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Sid Vicious and Questions About the Murder of Nancy Spungen

podcast.title: Limited Repertoire – Nine Songs Repeated
podcast.body: The Vicious White Kids had a limited repertoire, consisting of just nine songs. For their three sets at the Electric Ballroom, they simply repeated these nine songs three times. "They had just nine songs. So for the three sets, they just repeated them three times."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Nancy Spungin's Attempted Backing Vocals
podcast.body: Nancy Spungin insisted on singing backup vocals at the Vicious White Kids' gig, but the sound engineer deliberately turned off her microphone. "He insisted on singing backup vocals, but the sound guy made sure her mic was turned off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Sid Vicious and Questions About the Murder of Nancy Spungen

podcast.title: Post-Sex Pistols Project
podcast.body: Before his death, Sid Vicious was attempting to launch a career independent of the Sex Pistols with a new band called The Vicious White Kids. Some recordings from this project exist. "Before he died, Sid was trying to launch a post-Sexpistols career with a band called The Vicious White Kids."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock
